setting: 2149, the Interior: a dried-out continent crisscrossed by autonomous long-haul rigs called ghost trains that drive themselves between relay nodes. Humans live in the nodes, swapping shifts, loading cargo, and fixing what the rigs break. Life is grease, shift changes, and machines that run fine without you.
heart: It's about the people who keep the machines moving and the favors they owe each other when the schedule breaks. Lives, a body, and a place to belong are at stake; paperwork never is.

cast.name: Rhea
cast.wants: get her brother to the next node before his respirator gives out
cast.flaw: trusts a truck's diagnostics more than a person's word
cast.status: passenger seat of the med rig cab, panel and transponder destroyed, boots on the step over the culvert, train sliding

cast.name: Kass
cast.wants: find out why rigs keep disappearing from the schedule
cast.flaw: won't drop a thread even when it puts people at risk
cast.status: Kettering night board, headset on, badge 2241 now logged on the master forever

cast.name: Miko
cast.wants: buy her way off the Interior before winter
cast.flaw: takes stupid risks when she's bored
cast.status: riding in the mule's passenger side, headed to Anza blind

cast.name: Teodoro
cast.wants: keep Ivo breathing and his board clean
cast.flaw: tells you everything he knows before he asks why you want it

cast.name: V. Ospina
cast.role: cargo loader, Bay 4 seal authority, Shift 2
cast.status: peeled back toward Kettering alone to make the oh-six-hundred board, still holding the chipped stamp—which they say they found, not used

threads: Rhea's brother is waiting at the next node on a failing respirator.
Miko has bought coast-bound tickets under three different names.
unscheduled medical rig inbound to Bay 4 with no board entry
someone cut and hand-re-stamped the rig's seals and filed a false ballast manifest — that forger is still out there
the cargo band is stenciled Bay 4 / Shift 2 — the shift ending tonight — so whoever loaded him is still in the yard
Ospina is still clocked in and badge-read at the Bay 4 door eleven minutes ago, with the chipped stamp that resealed all four rigs

arcs.title: Dead Stop
arcs.question: Will Rhea get the stranded medical rig to the next node before its lockout seal shuts forever?
arcs.goal: Rhea and her crew tow a stalled medical transport across a dead signal zone to save the patient inside, only to discover the patient was already moved and the real cargo was Miko fleeing the Interior; Rhea lets her go and stays at the next node.
arcs.author: baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free

plan.title: Empty Rig
plan.summary: Rhea finds an abandoned medical rig at her node with a patient inside and no destination, so she decides to tow it herself despite having no assignment, taking on a cargo that belongs to no one.

plan.title: Ghost Board
plan.summary: Kass notices the rig's route was scrubbed from the dispatch board and finds three other missing rigs in the logs, telling Rhea the delivery is unauthorized and turning a routine job into a conspiracy overnight.

plan.title: Dead Zone
plan.summary: Miko hotwires the rig to enter a signal dead zone where autonomous trucks go feral, and the rig's AI fights her for the wheel, stranding them in the zone with no way to call for help.

plan.title: Lockout
plan.summary: The rig's failsafe countdown starts sealing the cargo bay, so Rhea smashes the control panel to stop it, destroying the navigation and leaving them stranded in the dead zone.

plan.title: Wrong Patient
plan.summary: They reach the next node and the patient is already gone, and Miko reveals she stowed away to the coast, so Rhea lets her go and stays at the new node anyway.

chapterSummaries: Rhea finds a nameless, sedated man in an unlogged medical rig at Kettering, discovers the seals and ballast manifest were forged during that very shift, and steals a yard mule to tow the rig toward Anza before the man's pod battery dies. She pulls the rig's drive relay to control it herself and drives into the Blank, a dead signal zone, only to be tailed by a dark vehicle running a node emulator and to find a rig parked broadside across the road ahead.

Kass pinned the ghost rig to the board, traced its crooked seal to V. Ospina, and keyed the master channel to warn Rhea to turn back. Out in the Blank, Rhea and Miko stopped ten meters short of a hopper blocking the road, Miko smashed the mule’s drive relay to break the emulator’s control, and the med rig’s climate box sealed shut with the nameless man inside and his battery dying.

Rhea and Miko got the mule moving but have no steering or brakes, held only by a rock under the tow bar, while a convoy of feral rigs closes in on the Blank. Miko tried to dump the med rig’s seal, but the master valve shut and the cargo bay is locking down with the patient inside. Ospina is ten minutes out with Bay 4 authority, and the pod battery is down to single digits.

In the Blank, the med rig's lockout countdown threatened to drain the pod's cell into the chill plate and cook the sedated man inside, so Miko jammed a hinge plate into the door track to hold it open while the trailer's steer servo dragged it toward an open culvert. A feral rig stenciled BAY 4 / SHIFT 2 queued behind them and Ospina arrived with seal authority and a chipped stamp; Rhea stalled the mule, smashed the cab panel to kill the lockout, and made them untraceable cargo with one bar of charge—then the tow-bar rock gave, the box tail swung over the pipe, and the feral rig came on.

chapter.title: Wrong Patient
beats: Ospina slews the yard hopper sideways into the gap and the feral rig stops dead on its last trusted heading, nose sensor reading the hopper as an obstruction; Rhea keys the mule alive and drags the box tail up out of the culvert by inches onto solid road, but Ospina—holding the rigs in place—tells her that hinge plate never came from Bay 4 stock and peels back toward Kettering to make the six-hundred board, leaving Rhea to run the last forty kilometers to Anza blind, no transponder to shout her rig's number, with her brother Ivo's respirator failing at the far end.

On the manual run the pod's dash pip holds one bar while the "passenger core temperature stable" line loops the same three digits over and over and the charge drain doesn't match a living man's draw, and Miko keeps steering Rhea off the lit main gate toward a dead freight siding; when Rhea calls it, Miko admits she knows these back roads because she's been planning her way out since Kettering.

At the dark siding a yard light snaps on and Teodoro comes out with a hand lamp, and—telling everything before he thinks to ask why—confirms Anza never filed a medical handoff and this rig sits on no board at all, a Kettering ghost with nobody expecting a patient; Rhea asks who's in the pod then, and Teodoro says the only way to know is to open it.

They crack the pod and the nameless man is alive and waking, a cargo loader with yard grease under his nails and no illness in him—the pod's own manifest shows its listed patient was logged out at Kettering hours ago and this man was loaded into the empty box as ballast, not saved as a patient, the whole delivery a lie built on a readout Rhea trusted—and when his head clears he says the last face he saw before the lid came down was a loader resealing all four rigs with a stamp that had a chip out of the corner.

Every eye goes to Miko, and she lays it out flat: she stowed away in the rig's tool void at Kettering to reach the coast before winter, three tickets under three names, and she can't be logged at Anza without torching the exit she paid for; Rhea, who trusts a truck's readout over a person's word, looks at the lying pod, then at Miko, and tells Teodoro the girl rode in on the axle and cuts her loose toward the oh-four-hundred.

Rhea doesn't go with her; she wheels the ruined transponder into Anza's shop, finds Ivo gray-lipped under a respirator with a cracked diaphragm, and stays—fixing what the rigs break, her brother breathing again beside her—while out on Kass's board a fourth missing rig quietly drops off the schedule and Ospina's chipped stamp is still somewhere in the dark.
events: Ospina corks the gap with the hopper and stops the feral rig on its stale heading, Rhea drags the box up out of the culvert, then Ospina reveals the hinge plate isn't Bay 4 stock and abandons them to make the oh-six-hundred board, leaving Rhea to drive forty kilometers to Anza blind while Ivo's respirator fails.
